newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-CLUB PRESIDENT WANTS "TREACHEROUS" REFEREE IN PRISON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CLUB PRESIDENT WANTS "TREACHEROUS" REFEREE IN PRISON.

text.p: The president of Spanish division one newcomers Extremadura thinks that "treacherous" referees are behind his team's failure to get a single point in the opening six games of the league championship.
"That kind of referee should be in prison," said Pedro Nieto after seeing several penalty appeals turned down in Wednesday's match against Racing Santander.
Extremadura saw hopes of winning their first-ever point at the top level dashed when Racing broke away to score the winner just five minutes from time.
Nieto has refused to apologise for his comments despite the near-certainty of action from the league disciplinary commitee.
"Speaking like that is the only way they listen to you," said Nieto in remarks published by the sports daily As on Friday.
Extremadura have lost all six matches, and are firmly anchored at the bottom of the first division having let in 17 goals while scoring just three.
Despite the run of defeats, support is still strong in the team's home town of Almendralejo, where crowds average nearly a third of the 25,000 population.
The club's annual budget, of around 900 million pesetas ($7 million) is dwarfed by those of big clubs like Barcelona and Real Madrid, who have ten times as much money to play with.
